title: SDLC Plugin Manifest
description: Schema for plugins/<name>/manifest.yaml — the machine-read declarative profile the pipeline-orchestrator consumes (human docs live in the plugin README.md). `kind: foundation` is a stack provider that owns platform aspects and drives phases; `kind: framework` is an additive library provider that enriches existing phases. The aspect enums ($defs.platformAspect / functionalAspect) MIRROR plugins/sdlc/config/aspects.yaml — keep them in sync.

allOf.description: A framework names its library via `dependency` (or, as an escape hatch, ships `detect`); a foundation detects by project structure via `detect`.

then.description: Framework (additive) manifests enrich existing phases. They MUST declare `enriches_aspect` and MUST NOT declare `workflow` / `framework_detection` / `hosts_aspects` / `agents_per_phase` / `on_demand_agents` / `aar_analyst` / a non-empty `aspects`.

Foundation (stack provider) manifests own platform aspects and drive phases. They detect by project structure and MUST NOT declare `enriches_aspect` / `dependency` (those are a framework's shorthand).

kind.description: `foundation` = stack provider: owns platform aspect(s), hosts frameworks, carries per-role expertise (`role_expertise`) and a default workflow. `framework` = additive: enriches existing phases, points at one functional aspect via enriches_aspect. Neither ships agents — the core plugin owns the whole roster and binds it in its own manifest's agents_per_phase (ADR-0021).

stack.description: Unique stack id. Lowercase, alphanumeric + hyphens.

priority.description: 0 = vanilla fallback. 100+ = stack provider. Higher wins per platform aspect. For frameworks this is documentational only — they never compete for an aspect.

aspects.description: Foundation only: PLATFORM / WINNER aspects this profile OWNS — the axis for per-aspect winner resolution (`android` for the foundation; `backend`/`frontend`/… for web stacks). NOT the functional library taxonomy.

enriches_aspect.description: Framework only: the single FUNCTIONAL category this framework decorates (network, persistence, di, ui, background, analytics, architecture). The framework attaches under whichever FOUNDATION's `hosts_aspects` includes this category — no specific plugin named.

hosts_aspects.description: Foundation only: the FUNCTIONAL categories this foundation accepts frameworks for. Either the literal `all` (every category in aspects.yaml) or an explicit subset. A framework attaches when its `enriches_aspect` is hosted here AND its `dependency` is found via `framework_detection`. MUST be declared together with `framework_detection` (a foundation that accepts categories must also say where to look, and vice versa).

framework_detection.description: Foundation only: the ordered list of files/globs where the orchestrator searches for a framework's `dependency` coordinate, ON THIS FOUNDATION'S BEHALF (0b-frameworks). The foundation owns WHERE to look (e.g. ['gradle/libs.versions.toml','**/build.gradle.kts','**/build.gradle']); the core owns only the substring-matching mechanics.

dependency.description: Framework only: the library coordinate(s) that signal this framework is in use — e.g. 'com.squareup.retrofit2'. The plugin just NAMES it; the hosting foundation declares WHERE to look and the orchestrator executes the search. A list matches if ANY coordinate is found.

workflow.description: Foundation only: default workflow recipe selected when this is the PRIMARY profile and neither --workflow=NAME nor sdlc.local.yaml active_workflow is given.

detect.description: Auto-detect rules. Use `any` for OR, `all` for AND. Required for foundations; optional escape hatch for frameworks not identified by a single coordinate.

agents_per_phase.description: CORE manifest only (plugins/sdlc/manifest.yaml): phase → agent name (aspect-agnostic) or phase → {aspect: agent name} (aspect-aware fan-out). Deprecated for foundations since ADR-0021 — honored with a WARN for one release, then ignored; foundations carry `role_expertise` instead. Frameworks must not declare it.

on_demand_agents.description: CORE manifest only: agents invoked directly, NOT by a workflow phase (debugger, devops, cicd, aar-analyst). They receive their stack expertise via `resolve/cli.mjs expertise --role`. Deprecated for foundations since ADR-0021.

aar_analyst.description: DEPRECATED (ADR-0021): agent name that overrode the core `aar-analyst` for /sdlc:aar. Honored for one release; the core `aar-analyst` now receives the stack's `role_expertise.aar-analyst` instead. Will be removed from the schema.

convention_skills.description: Fully-qualified `plugin:skill` ids to apply during development (and other phases as the agent sees fit). Merged across the foundation and active frameworks.

extra_phases.description: Phases to insert into the workflow at an `after:` anchor. Usually empty for both foundations and frameworks.

agent.description: The CORE role that runs the phase — the only way a foundation adds a phase now that it binds no agents (ADR-0021).

pre_phase_commands.description: Shell commands to run before phases begin. Usually empty.

phase_injections.description: Per-phase prompt-injection text the orchestrator concatenates into the phase prompt (held internally as `phase_prompts_injection`). Keys are phase names (`development`, `security`, `qa`, …); values are block-scalar guidance strings.

post_pipeline_checks.description: Shell commands run after the pipeline (lint/test/compile gates). Empty for most frameworks.

heal_checks.description: Shell commands the G1 self-healing loop runs after a guarded phase (compile/lint gates ONLY — never unit tests). Merged across profiles as a de-duplicated union, PRIMARY first. Usually a subset of post_pipeline_checks. Empty for most frameworks.

role_expertise.description: ADR-0021: per-ROLE platform expertise the CORE agents consume. Keys are core agent names ($defs.coreRole). The resolver merges every active manifest's block (foundation first, frameworks alphabetically by stack), renders `invariants` + `rules` into the `Stack expertise for <role>` block the orchestrator pastes into the phase prompt's stable prefix, and `skills` into the deduped `Skills for this role` list; `resolve/cli.mjs expertise --role` prints the same for an on-demand agent. `rules` paths are relative to THIS manifest's directory and are emitted absolute (the reading agent lives in another plugin, where ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} would resolve wrong). Budget: `invariants` ≤ 1400 chars (~300 tokens) per role — it rides in every turn's prefix.

invariants.description: Short, always-on rules for this role on this stack. Present by construction in every dispatch — keep it to the non-negotiables; long checklists belong in a skill.

rules.description: Rule files the agent may `Read` (paths relative to this manifest's directory). A `note` says when to read it.

skills.description: Skills this role must (mandatory, the default) or may (recommended) invoke — the same row shape as sdlc.local.yaml `extensions.skills`, deduped with them, strictest policy wins.

when.description: The moment to invoke it, e.g. 'before the first Write/Edit of production Kotlin'.

coreRole.description: The agent roster the CORE plugin ships (plugins/sdlc/agents/*.md) — the only roles a `role_expertise` block may address (ADR-0021). MIRRORS the values of plugins/sdlc/manifest.yaml `agents_per_phase` ∪ `on_demand_agents` — keep them in sync.

platformAspect.description: PLATFORM / WINNER aspect — what a foundation owns and competes to win. MIRRORS plugins/sdlc/config/aspects.yaml `platform`.

functionalAspect.description: FUNCTIONAL / LIBRARY aspect — the cross-cutting category a framework addresses. MIRRORS plugins/sdlc/config/aspects.yaml `functional`.

file_exists.description: Path (relative to project root) that must exist.

path.description: Path relative to project root. May be a glob — matches when ANY globbed file contains the pattern. Glob honors .gitignore.

pattern.description: Regex evaluated against the file contents.

file_glob.description: Glob pattern (relative to project root). Matches if at least one file matches.

oneOf.description: Nested OR — matches if any sub-rule matches.
Nested AND — matches only if every sub-rule matches.
